Calibrate many basins in one batch

Source: R/batch.R
calibrate_batch.Rd

Runs the same calibration protocol on every basin in a folder, giving each basin its own calibration-log project, so every calibration is recorded, can be reviewed, and is done exactly the same way. The batch can be stopped at any time, by a crash, a power cut or on purpose, and started again with the same call: each basin carries on from the last step it completed. Steps already in a basin's log are never repeated, so a finished basin passes through in moments; a step newly asked for, such as the test, is added. Changing the protocol does not recalibrate a basin that already has a calibration: its log keeps the calibration it had.

Usage

calibrate_batch(
  basins,
  output,
  structure = NULL,
  overrides = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  objective = c("nse", "rmse", "log_rmse"),
  starts = 10L,
  seed = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 200),
  method = c("lbfgsb", "nelder_mead"),
  staged = FALSE,
  test = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  only = NULL,
  owner = "Not recorded",
  steward = "Not recorded",
  purpose = "Batch calibration"
)

batch_status(output)

batch_results(output)

Arguments

basins

Folder holding one subfolder per basin.

output

Folder for the projects and the status file; created if needed.

structure

Default configuration (a list or YAML path) for basins whose basin.yml names none; the standard PDM if NULL. The basin's area is always applied.

overrides, exclude

Passed to calibration_bounds().

objective, starts, seed, control, method

Passed to calibrate_pdm(). Search scales come from the bounds table.

staged

If TRUE, calibrate in stages, as calibrate_staged() does, with stages from pdm_stages(): one auto_calibration entry per stage. An interrupted basin resumes from its last finished stage. objective then applies to no stage; each stage has its own.

test

If TRUE, score each validated candidate once on its test window, if it has one. Use it when the protocol is final; the test window is scored only once.

cores

Number of basins to run at once, in parallel worker processes.

only

Optional basin identifiers to run, for example to retry failures.

owner, steward, purpose

Recorded in each new project.

Value

calibrate_batch(): the batch status, invisibly, as from batch_status(). batch_status(): a data.table with one row per basin: basin, state (queued, running, done or failed), step reached, seconds and message. batch_results(): read_projects() for every project, with the batch state.

Details

Input folder. One subfolder per basin, named by its identifier, holding:

  • forcing.csv: columns time (ISO 8601, UTC), rain and pet in mm per interval;

  • flow.csv: column q_m3s (and optionally time), aligned with the forcing;

  • basin.yml: area_km2 and calibration (start and end) are required; catchment, gauge, validation, test, config (a YAML configuration file in the folder), headline, thresholds (a list of name, value, unit), rating (a CSV in the folder) and snow are optional.

Snow. For a basin with snow: true in basin.yml, forcing.csv also needs a temperature column (deg C), and rain holds all precipitation. The PACK snow model turns them into the rain and melt reaching the ground, with fixed parameters: the default preset, or a preset named by snow, or a PACK YAML file in the basin folder named by snow. PACK is not calibrated; only the PDM is. The series PACK produces is registered as the rain, and a note in the log records the PACK parameters and the checksum of the original forcing.

Steps for each basin, each written to its project as it completes: start the project, register the data, select the structure, run the automatic calibration, propose the best result as candidate, validate it, and, with test = TRUE, test it once on the test window.

Progress. batch-status.csv in the output folder gets a row whenever a basin starts, finishes or fails; batch_status() summarises it while the batch runs. A failure is recorded with its reason and the batch moves on; fix the cause and run the same call again.

Seeds. Each basin's random starts are seeded from seed and the basin's name, so a basin's result does not change when others are added or removed.

See also

calibration_log, compare_structures(), calibration_bounds()
